findings.title: Retry increments can be lost when cron runs overlap
findings.body: The retry count is written as `reminder.retryCount + 1` from the value loaded before scheduling. If two cron invocations process the same reminder concurrently and both scheduling attempts fail, both write the same increment rather than accumulating two failures. This can keep the reminder below the deletion threshold and cause it to be retried indefinitely; use an atomic database increment (and consider claiming reminders before processing).
